d: Parco del castello del Conte d'Almaviva, which has a façade: on one side there is a large door adorned with the coat of arms of the Count engorged with flowers, on the other there is a large arch that puts to a boulevard, and from which hang festoons and garlands. Some villagers end up adorning the place: meanwhile comes a choir of Vassalli del Conte accompanied by a drappello of Villanelle all dressed as parties, singinging and jumping.
Don Alvaro, Plagio and sayings.
Figaro comes out of the castle. Everyone goes to meet him; he observes the arrangement of the place, indicates from one to the other etc.
Figaro and Plagio.
The Count leaves the castle: he has letters in his hand, which he reads carefully. Figaro from time to time shows himself aside, and listens.
Figaro solo.
They come out accompanied and celebrated by the Choir the Countess, Inez and Susanna.
Figaro and said, "The Count."
A Servant and sayings, then Cherubino.
Figaro, go to Plagio.
Atrium of the castle. Cherubino solo, indi Inez.
He enters Figaro in tiptoe and stands aside in the position of one who listens, and sayings.
Cherubim takes the air of an irritated man: Inez of those who listen mortified. Meanwhile, the Count and Figaro slowly come out.
Figaro solo, in the Plagio.
Garden in the Count's castle with vegetable caves. Inez only stealthy looking here and there, in the south of Susanna.
The Count and Figaro (from the opposite side to the one for which they left Inez and Susanna).
Cherubino and Susanna and the two hidden.
The Countess and Inez on the one hand with Servi, Paesani on the other hastily.
Park as in the first act. Paesani and Villanelle coming out of the castle talking to each other.
Plagio and sayings.
Susanna from the castle.
Figaro and dicto.
Plagio and sayings.
I'm just plagiarizing.

An anteroom for the use of a wardrobe that he puts in Susanna's room. From here and there are two closets, in one of which he starts one of those wooden tools, to which he hangs his clothes, covered by a Ferraiolo and a hat. Susanna and Inez entering quickly, in the direction of Cherubino.
Figaro entering furiously and sayings, then the Count and the Countess.
The Count and Figaro.
The Count, ind Susanna with a burden under her arm.
Gallery. Some servants introduce Don Alvaro, then the Count.
The Countess, Inez and sayings.
The Count and Don Alvaro.
Figaro introducing the Notaro, then Plagio.
The Count, Don Alvaro, and Plagio.
Figaro and sayings, then the Notaro who returns.
Choir of Vassalli, then the Countess, Inez, Susanna and sayings.
Cherubino dressed as a colonel comes in suddenly.
